The Burden of Inheritable Disabilities on Society

Individuals with inheritable disabilities—such as cystic fibrosis, Huntington’s disease, sickle cell anemia, and Down syndrome—often face severe physical and cognitive impairments. While some argue that individuals with disabilities should have the right to reproduce, the reality is that most of these conditions are incompatible with a healthy, productive life. Many individuals with severe genetic disorders cannot care for themselves, let alone raise children. Even those with milder conditions often face significant cognitive or physical limitations that make independent reproduction difficult.

Critics of eugenic policies often argue that such measures are inherently discriminatory, but the reality is that preventing the spread of genetic diseases is not about eliminating people—it is about preventing suffering. Many of these conditions are incurable and devastating, and allowing their propagation would lead to an endless cycle of preventable suffering.

Consider Huntington’s disease, a fatal neurodegenerative disorder with no cure. If an individual with Huntington’s disease reproduces, their children have a 50% chance of inheriting the condition. If left unchecked, it will continue to affect more and more individuals, overwhelming healthcare systems. While some may argue that preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) and genetic counseling can prevent the transmission of harmful traits, these methods are not foolproof. Additionally, PGT is expensive and not universally accessible, meaning that those who can afford it may still reproduce, while others are left with no option but to pass on the condition.

Mandatory sterilization policies, when applied to individuals with clearly inheritable and severe conditions, provide a last line of defense against the spread of genetic diseases.   2. Informed consent – Individuals must be fully aware of the consequences before sterilization is enforced.

The debate over mandatory sterilization for individuals with inheritable disabilities is not about eliminating people—it is about protecting the future of humanity from preventable suffering.
